content.text: {"route":"gap","reason":"The record leaves material questions open and the agency's analysis rests on unexamined premises. (1) Reprisal knowledge: S1 denied knowing of prior EEO activity, but Complainant's cited activity was a grievance of the FY2020 rating to the Commander, and S2 and HR were involved in changing it. The record does not test whether S1 knew of that grievance or its outcome, and it does not address whether the grievance is protected EEO activity. (2) Comparators: the FDD faulted Complainant for lacking comparators, yet the record does not identify the other division chiefs, their performance, or their treatment. Meeting attendance rests only on S1 and the Deputy Commander's statements that all leaders were invited. (3) Medical request: S1 said two subordinates were also asked for notes, but those individuals are not identified and have no affidavits or documentation. The physician's note allowed telework and did not address the one-day in-office policy, and the record does not show whether the policy was documented or applied uniformly. (4) Performance reasons: colleague statements conflict, and S2 said documentation was insufficient for a '1.' The FY2021 threat is only denied by S1, with no documentary or witness evidence on what was said at the March 18 meeting. (5) The FDD's account of the HR reason for the rating change (a PIP was required) differs from the S2 statement in the record that documentation was insufficient. There is also no developed analysis of the national origin, race, disability or harassment bases, or of the Hispanic/race issue. The record cannot support a reliable merits decision without further development."}
